The residents, who spoke with LEADERSHIP in Ibadan, called on the state government, NURTW leadership and other stakeholders to urgently initiate peaceful measures to prevent a crisis. The tension followed disagreements between the state government and the union over the interpretation of a recent Court of Appeal judgment. While the government insists that the judgment does not automatically grant NURTW the right to seize public motor parks, the union maintains that the ruling has restored its rights and insists on enforcing it. A resident, Mr Tanimomo Ajao, urged both parties to prioritise peace and prevent bloodshed ahead of the November 23 deadline. He called on key stakeholders to initiate legal clarification and dialogue to ensure an objective interpretation of the court judgment. Ajao urged the state government to convene an emergency peace meeting involving NURTW leaders, Alhaji Abideen Olajide and Comrade Lekan Alesinloye, leaders of the Park Management System (PMS), and neutral arbiters, including the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and civil society organisations. He also called on the state Commissioner of Police, the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) and the General Officer Commanding (GOC), who had already been alerted by the union, to deploy joint security teams to volatile garages and major motor parks across the state’s 33 local government areas to prevent attempts at forceful enforcement. “Security agencies must make it clear that any attempt by union members or PMS loyalists to forcefully take over parks on November 23 will be treated as a breach of public peace and met with lawful resistance,” he said. Rather than an abrupt takeover or outright resistance, Ajao urged the government and NURTW to negotiate a structured framework and timeline for any lawful reorganisation of park management. He said such an arrangement should accommodate displaced workers and PMS operators to prevent gang violence and territorial disputes. He also called on the state government to issue a clear public statement explaining how it intended to comply with the appellate court judgment while protecting public safety and addressing growing concerns among residents. However, the NURTW state chairman, Alhaji Abideen Olajide, popularly known as Ejiogbe, insisted that the union would proceed with its planned takeover of public parks and garages across the state’s 33 local government areas on November 23. He argued that a recent Court of Appeal judgment had nullified the state government’s longstanding suspension and exclusion of the union. “We have threatened to self-enforce the judgment starting November 23,” he said. Olajide disclosed that the union had notified the Federal Government, the GOC of the Nigerian Army’s 2 Division, the DSS, the Oyo State Commissioner of Police and the NLC about its planned enforcement. But the state government has rejected the union’s interpretation of the judgment, warning that it would resist any attempt to take over public motor parks. The governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Dr Sulaimon Olanrewaju, said the judgment did not confer on NURTW the right to control or manage public motor parks. He maintained that any attempt to forcibly seize, occupy or interfere with the management of the facilities would be resisted through all lawful means. According to the government, the judgment merely reaffirmed citizens’ constitutional right to freedom of association and did not direct the state to hand over public motor parks to the union. “The judgment merely reaffirmed the constitutional right of citizens to freedom of association. “It did not confer ownership, control, or management of public assets on any union, nor did it authorise any organisation to take over facilities built, maintained, and regulated by government. “Accordingly, any attempt to rely on the judgment as a basis for demanding, threatening, or effecting the takeover of public motor parks is a clear misinterpretation of the court’s decision and has no basis in law,” he said.
